technical.summary: Strong trend structure with ADX confirmation, but momentum indicators show overbought conditions and recent bearish crossovers in MACD and Stochastic, limiting swing entry conviction.

fundamental.summary: WEC shows no insider buying conviction, no institutional accumulation signals, zero government contract activity, no lobbying engagement, and minimal retail interest; earnings in 10 days present elevated volatility risk with no fundamental support.

sentiment.summary: Extreme market fear (26/100) presents contrarian buy opportunity, but stale congressional data (449 days old) and absent news sentiment provide no confirmation.

risk.summary: Crisis VIX (418.4), flat yield curve, rising dollar, and earnings in 10 days create a highly adverse macro backdrop for WEC.

debate.key_bull_argument: Strong ADX trend structure with EMA 50/200 bullish alignment and contrarian fear-zone opportunity (VIX 26) provide directional conviction for trend followers.
debate.key_bear_argument: Overbought momentum (RSI 21, Stochastic), recent MACD/Stochastic bearish crossovers, price below EMA-9/TEMA, zero fundamental support, high earnings risk in 10 days, and crisis macro backdrop (VIX 418.4, rising USD, flat yield curve) create excessive downside risk that outweighs trend structure.

decision.entry_rationale: Strong ADX trend and EMA 50/200 bullish alignment provide directional structure, but overbought momentum indicators and bearish MACD/Stochastic crossovers signal exhaustion. Earnings in 10 days and crisis macro backdrop (VIX 418.4, rising USD) create unacceptable risk/reward for swing entry.
decision.primary_risk: Earnings volatility in 10 days combined with overbought technicals and macro headwinds could trigger sharp reversal, trapping swing longs with no fundamental support.
decision.agent_agreement: strong — technical, fundamental, risk, and debate all converge on bear case; only sentiment offers weak contrarian signal
decision.portfolio_note: Already holding WEC with 70 existing Utilities positions (19% of portfolio); concentration risk and sector saturation further reduce conviction for additional exposure.
